description:
Gate G0. No other astro-site-* item may start until this ADR is approved by the repo owner.

Write _project/decisions/adr-astro-unified-site.md. It must decide each of the following, giving the default below or a reasoned alternative:
D1 Package location: `website/` (NOT `site/`, which dlv2-60 reserves for routes.yml and which assemble_public_site.py already uses as its output dir).
D2 Explorer integration: results-explorer stays its own Vite+Preact package served at /results/ with substantial code reuse, not "unchanged". It needs:
- the shared header/shell extracted from App.tsx
- controlled global CSS
- query-string state kept
- deep links to nested /results/ routes on GitHub Pages
- worker/WASM asset paths and recovery verified in a browser
Docs and blog pages never download the Explorer runtime. Embeds come only after cutover (astro-site-60).
D3 URL policy: keep existing routes where practical, `.html` included. Measure quality with a reviewed URL compatibility report (astro-site-50): zero broken public URLs and zero broken fragments. Each redirect page (meta refresh + canonical; GitHub Pages cannot send 301s) is listed with a reason. There is no redirect-percentage threshold.
D4 Content source: docs/ stays the content directory. Until the renderer cutover, every page must build in both Sphinx and Astro from the same docs/ sources, so no converted output is committed and nothing is edited in two places.
D5 Versions: follow the dlv2-60 routes.yml manifest (/ and /docs/ from the latest release tag; /docs/dev/, /blog/ and /results/ from trunk). The API reference documents the released wheel, per adr-independent-publication-authorities. Hosting historical guide versions is a separate, out-of-scope decision.
D6 Layouts: a custom Astro shell for landing, blog and results. For docs, Starlight inside the shared shell is the default; custom docs layouts only if Starlight overrides prove brittle in the spike (G1).
D7 API reference: decided at gate astro-site-02. Curated, authored Markdown contracts for an explicit public-symbol list. No docstring dependency, and no archiving of removed prose (comment-policy.md).
D8 Feed: keep Atom at /blog/atom.xml with unchanged entry ids.
D9 Search: Pagefind for docs and blog HTML only. The first release's unified search covers docs and blog; results stay reachable through Explorer filtering. Static result summaries (astro-site-61) come later. Search indexes obey Explorer visibility and withdrawal rules.
D10 Tooling: Node 20 to match CI, an exact lockfile, and no root package.json unless the spike shows workspaces are needed.
D11 Blog drafts: _blog/ (109 md: research, outlines, archives) stays outside every published collection.
D12 Publication: the site plugs into the dlv2-60 site-deploy plane (adr-dev-loop-v2 D2) and keeps its artifact boundaries. Explorer code, corpus data, prose and API docs stay separately sourced and pinned, with provenance, privacy checks, route digests, receipts and rollback-by-receipt.
D13 Atomic renderer cutover: production never serves a mixed Sphinx/Astro artifact. Sphinx renders every route until a release tag contains website/ plus all migrated content. At that release one site-deploy run switches landing, stable docs, dev docs, blog and results to Astro together. Astro then renders stable content from the release tag and dev content from trunk. Site-deploy assembly must refuse an artifact whose routes use different renderers.
D14 Overlapping work: assign ownership and order before implementation:
- comment-cleanup-site-assets and comment-cleanup-generators must not remove landing/, Sphinx assets or generator behaviour that the dual-build depends on.
- dlv2-61 (docs.yml retirement) must not remove a fallback before astro-site-54.
- Docstring-removal work must not run ahead of the astro-site-02 contract source SHA.
Record each overlapping item's agreed scope or deferral in the ADR, and get owner sign-off.
Also list the global guardrails (see context) and the stop conditions for abandoning the migration.
